skill: i want to learn how to host my own minecraft server

route.title: Join Someone Else's Server First
route.summary: Before hosting your own, you need to understand what a multiplayer server feels like. Join a public Minecraft server and play for 20 minutes. Notice how you connect, what the server rules are, and how other players interact.

challenge.prompt: Write 3 sentences about the server you joined. What was its name? What did you do there? Did you see other players?

route.title: Find Your Computer's Local IP Address
route.summary: Every device on your home network has an IP address, like a house number. You'll need yours to test your server. On Windows, open Command Prompt and type 'ipconfig'. On Mac, open Terminal and type 'ifconfig'. Look for something like 192.168.1.5.

challenge.prompt: Take a screenshot showing your local IP address on your screen. Circle or point to the number that starts with 192.168 or 10.0.

route.title: Download and Run the Minecraft Server File
route.summary: Go to minecraft.net/download/server and download the server.jar file. Put it in a new folder called 'MyMinecraftServer'. Double-click it to run. It will create some files and stop. Open eula.txt, change 'false' to 'true', and run server.jar again. When it says 'Done', your server is running.

challenge.prompt: Take a screenshot of the server window showing the message 'Done' and the blinking cursor where you can type commands.

route.title: Connect to Your Own Server Locally
route.summary: Open Minecraft Java Edition. Click Multiplayer, then Add Server. For the address, type 'localhost'. Join the server. You should spawn in a new world that YOUR computer is running. Walk around, break some blocks, place a sign with your name.

challenge.prompt: Take a screenshot in Minecraft showing you standing next to a sign you placed that says your name or 'My Server'.

route.title: Let a Friend on Your Network Join
route.summary: If someone else is on your home WiFi, they can join using your local IP from waypoint 2. Give them the IP address (like 192.168.1.5) and have them add it as a server. When they connect, both of you should be in the same world.

challenge.prompt: Describe what happened when someone tried to join. Did it work? What did you both do together? If nobody could join, explain what error message appeared.

route.title: Edit server.properties to Change Your World
route.summary: Stop your server by typing 'stop' in the server window. Open the file 'server.properties' with Notepad or TextEdit. Find 'gamemode=survival' and change it to 'gamemode=creative'. Find 'difficulty=easy' and change it to 'difficulty=hard'. Save and restart your server.

challenge.prompt: Take a screenshot of your server.properties file showing gamemode=creative and difficulty=hard with those exact lines visible.

route.title: Give Yourself Operator Powers
route.summary: Operators (ops) can use special commands. While your server is running, type 'op YourMinecraftUsername' in the server console (replace with your actual username). Now join your server and type '/gamemode survival' in the Minecraft chat. You should switch modes instantly.

challenge.prompt: Take a screenshot in Minecraft after you used a slash command. The chat should show the command you typed and the result.

route.title: Find Your Public IP and Understand Port Forwarding
route.summary: Your public IP is how the internet sees your home network. Google 'what is my ip' to find it. For friends outside your home to join, you need to forward port 25565 on your router to your computer's local IP. This tells incoming Minecraft traffic where to go. Look up 'port forwarding' plus your router brand.

challenge.prompt: Write down your public IP address and explain in your own words what port forwarding does. Why can't outside friends join without it?

route.title: Set Up Port Forwarding on Your Router
route.summary: Log into your router (usually by typing 192.168.1.1 in a browser). Find the Port Forwarding section. Create a rule that forwards port 25565 to your computer's local IP. Save it. This is the hardest technical step—ask an adult if you get stuck.

challenge.prompt: Take a screenshot of your router's port forwarding page showing a rule for port 25565 pointing to your local IP address.

route.title: Test External Access
route.summary: Give a friend your public IP address (from waypoint 8). Have them add your server using that IP. If it works, they'll connect from outside your home network. If not, double-check your port forwarding and make sure your server is running.

challenge.prompt: Did your friend successfully connect from outside your home? Describe what happened. If it didn't work, what troubleshooting steps did you try?

route.title: Install Your First Plugin or Mod
route.summary: Vanilla servers are fine, but plugins add features. Download Paper (a server software that runs plugins) from papermc.io. Replace your server.jar with the Paper jar. Create a 'plugins' folder. Download a simple plugin like EssentialsX from essentialsx.net. Drop the plugin jar into the plugins folder and restart. Type '/plugins' in the server console to see it loaded.

challenge.prompt: Take a screenshot of your server console showing the output of the /plugins command with at least one plugin listed.

route.title: Create a Spawn Area and Server Rules
route.summary: Build a spawn area where players first appear—maybe a platform with signs explaining server rules, a path to resources, or a cool welcome structure. Use '/setworldspawn' while standing there to make it the official spawn point. Write at least 3 rules on signs.

challenge.prompt: Take a screenshot of your finished spawn area showing the structures you built and at least 3 rule signs that players will see when they join.
